subject: Getting predictions on natural scale for lognormal family

messages.author: b548117c8aed3bfb
messages.subject: Getting predictions on natural scale for lognormal family
parts:
Hello,
If I fit a model like
m1 <- inla(y ~x, family = "poisson", control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))
(A log-link Poisson GLM)
Then m1$summary.fitted.values will be on the count scale and m1$summary.linear.predictor will be on the log scale.
But if I do
m1 <- inla(y ~x, family = "lognormal", control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))
Both the linear predictor and the fitted values will be on the log scale.
Is there a way I can get predictions on the natural scale for a lognormal model?
My motivation is that I want to account for retransformation bias when calculating predictions (and the CIs) for y.
ie ln(y) = a + bx + error;
so predictions for y need to account for the error, so:
y = exp(a + bx)*exp(error)
Thanks
Chris

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Getting predictions on natural scale for lognormal family
parts:
yes, the reason is, as you say, that its simply just

log(y) ~ Normal(,)

so the link is the identity:

> inla.models()$likelihood$lognormal$link
[1] "default" "identity"
>

if you want results on the exp-scale, you have to transform them
manually, like densitites with inla.tmarginal(exp, marginal), or just
doing exp on the quantiles, like on the linear predictor.

if you want predictions on the data-level, its easiest to use sampling,
like inla.posterior.sample() and inla.posterior.sample.eval(), as we
adding new data from a given likelihood is not implemented.

Best
H

Just an additional comment...

the expected value of a lognormal is (\mu + \sigma^{2}/2), where \mu and \sigma are the mean and standard deviation.
